specs.value: 180 W max with fan; 110 W without fan
16,600 lm at 180 W; about 10,000 lm without fan
520 × 240 mm; 23 mm high without fan, 42 mm with fan
Smart fan, switches on at 38 °C and off at 33 °C
Bluetooth via My Chihiros app (brightness, colour mix, timer, sunrise/sunset, fan)
2 m power cable, 3.8 m LED cable, 2 × 2 m steel hanging cables

fits.fact: Sized for tanks up to about 90 cm long. A 180 cm tank can use two units side by side, grouped in the app.
Meant for planted and aquascape tanks that need strong light and good colour rendering.
Not for tanks with a cover. It must hang at least 60 mm above the water, and it is for indoor use only.
The optional shades only block light at the front and back, so light still spills out the sides. This can bother people in living-room setups, for example near a TV.

usage.fact: Hang it from the ceiling with the included steel cables, or use a separate holder. Vietnamese shops sell the stand separately.
The cooling fan has to be attached to get the full 180 W. Without it, the light is limited to about 110 W.
First setup: install My Chihiros, turn on Bluetooth and location on your phone, pick the light from the device list, then set the colours.
Chihiros staff advise 20–30% brightness for a new planted tank, then about 5% more every 1–2 weeks. In a mature tank, use a preset and adjust it by about ±5%.
Recommended light period is 6–8 hours, with the light 15–30 cm above the water.
When buying online in Vietnam, the shop recommends filming the unboxing in case you need to make a warranty claim.

issues.fact: Long-term reports are scarce. One owner gave it 4 stars because they weren't yet sure how long it would last.
On the earlier Vivid RGB, forum users argued about fan noise and worried the light could fail if the fan did.
The light is very intense, so expect to spend time fine-tuning it. A user of the older RGB Vivid also called its mounting hardware poor.
Version difference: the Vivid III is thinner than the Vivid II (2.3 cm vs 3.4 cm) and goes up from 130 W to 180 W.
Vua Qua's 6-month warranty doesn't cover the power supply, and its refund value drops each month after the first.
Spec listings don't agree on the LED count: Vua Qua's page gives both 40/80 and 160/160.

alternatives.why: Cheaper and an older generation at about 5,500,000₫ on Vua Qua. It is thicker and less powerful (about 125–130 W).
Much cheaper rail-style light with less output (74 W, 6,630 lm) for 60–80 cm tanks. It suits lower-tech planted tanks.
Budget option at 67 W. Chihiros replacement parts for this line are sold at Vietnamese shops such as Shrimp Home.
